title: Albion Online Black Zone Gathering Guide
author: Elivaras
summary: Black Zone gathering is one of Albion Online's most reliable high-risk, high-reward professions. The Black Zone uses full-loot PvP, so another player can take your carried equipment and inventory when they kill you. You will eventually lose a set. The goal is not to make every trip deathless - it is

uses full-loot PvP, so another player can take your carried equipment and inventory when they kill you. You will eventually lose a set. The goal is not to make every trip deathless - it is to prepare well enough, spot danger early enough and bank consistently enough that successful trips comfortably pay for the losses.

Start with a set and mount you can afford to replace at least ten times.

Bank once your carried value reaches the cost of your full loadout, or exceeds the amount you are willing to lose.
Stay mounted whenever possible, inspect unfamiliar players and leave before a suspicious group can organise around you.

content: Which gathering journal should I bring?

children: Each gathering profession has journals from Tier 4 to Tier 8. An empty journal fills passively while you gather its matching resource, creating additional value from a trip you were already taking. Common T6 choices are:

A resource can fill a matching journal of its own tier or up to two tiers below it. For example, T6, T7 and T8 ore can fill a T6 Prospector's Journal, while T6 and T7 ore cannot fill a T8 journal. T7 and T8 journals are slower to fill because those resources are scarce, so T6 journals are a strong general choice for established
sessions. If your route is mostly T4-T6, bring lower-tier journals that match what you will actually gather.

Your access route determines which gear, tools and mounts make sense. Pick the operating model first, then build the set around it.

content: 1. Gather from guild territories or hideouts

children: Friendly territories and hideouts provide frequent safe exits.
Home zones deep in the Outlands can provide access to high-tier, high-quality zones.
Repeated local sweeps make slow-respawning T7 and T8 nodes easier to find.
Nearby allies can make mixed gathering and PvE sets more viable.
Friendly gatherers compete for the same nodes.
Low-tier or low-quality home zones may be disappointing.
Moving stock back to a Royal City can become a separate transport operation.

You can bring only the tools and gathering gear the destination requires. The weakness is travel time: better zones deeper in the Outlands are farther from portal towns, and every extra map creates another opportunity to meet scouts or roadblocks.

content: 4. Base yourself in a Smuggler's Den

children: independent gatherers who want a repeatable

Choose a den near high-tier zones but still within a tolerable transport distance of your main portal town. A local market helps replace supplies, while the safe entrance makes situational mounts more practical. Expect competition: solo players, small groups and gankers may all use the same den as a base.
For a fully solo player, a sensibly located Smuggler's Den is often the best long-term base. The SAFE Portal is the easiest way to begin without committing to a location.
Your strategy should change as your gathering progression improves.

wear the matching gathering cap and garb, then gather useful T4-T6 nodes for that resource. The gathering set improves yield and fame, while consistent nodes level faster than waiting for rare T7 or T8 spawns.

stay focused on your established line, roam between T6-T8 zones and prioritise valuable enchanted nodes. Once several lines reach T8, bring their tools and monetise more of every map.
What is the difference between resource nodes and resource mobs?
is a normal harvestable object such as a tree, ore deposit or fibre plant. A
carries harvestable resources but must be defeated before its remains can be gathered; hide animals are the most familiar example, while other resources also have matching creatures.
What are Dynamic Resource Hotspots and Resource Mists?
Dynamic Resource Hotspots concentrate many resource mobs of one type in a small area, so they are valuable but easier for other players to predict and contest.

Hotspot sites are recognisable, but the event at each site is temporary rather than permanently active. When a Dynamic Resource Hotspot is active, its resource icon appears over the location as you approach. Reaching one early can provide a dense group of matching resource mobs.

children: Some hotspots contain Verdant Wisps leading to a Resource Mist for that hotspot's resource. A Small Resource Mist is a solo instance; a Medium Resource Mist can contain other players, so treat it as lethal until you have confirmed the situation.
Check the middle of the map. Many gatherers hug the edges because they feel safer, leaving central nodes less contested.
Do not wait beside depleted T7 or T8 nodes. Their long, variable respawns make camping inefficient.
Use Roads of Avalon portals as optional connections to other high-tier zones, but inspect the route before committing.

Leave zones showing 16-30 players when you cannot see an activity or blob explaining the count.
Treat prime time as a deliberate risk choice. More activity can improve resource availability, but it also produces more organised gank groups.
Do not build routes around a respawn rumour

T7 and T8 node respawn timers change with activity and are difficult to
measure conclusively. Server reset can create a rush because nobody gathers
during downtime, but fixed hour-by-hour spawn claims should be treated as
anecdotal, not a timer.
Some ganks are not survivable. A coordinated group can cover every exit and dismount ahead of your route. Your aim is to make that level of coordination necessary.
Beginner tell: watch behaviour, not only gear

A scout's job is usually to maintain vision while partners move into position outside your screen. Treat a player as a possible scout when they mirror two direction changes, ride parallel instead of passing, wait between you and a safe exit, or disappear towards your likely route and return. Equipment is only a clue; repeated tracking behaviour is the stronger signal. You do not need proof to leave. Turn towards the route you already cleared, choose another exit or bank before the group can form ahead of you.
Every player you run into in the
is a possible threat. Constantly scan the edges of your screen for names of approaching players, and consider leaving immediately when spotted.

Learn common ganking signals. Examples include
If a player is dismounted and has no yellow mount-health bar, turn away immediately.
Keep game audio high enough to hear a nearby dismount or
Be aware that gatherers may leave vision, change into ganking equipment and return to attack you.

On a large node, remount periodically. If another player is dismounted nearby, the warning exclamation mark above your character gives you information you would miss by remaining dismounted until the node is empty.
Gather outside peak activity until you trust your own reactions.
Avoid travelling directly along the obvious road through a zone.
Do not contest a plentiful node when the map feels busy and you cannot identify the other players.
If a map suddenly fills without a matching blob, change map, use Journey Back, enter a Road, or wait inside suitable instanced content.
If gankers are visibly controlling the next zone's entrance, turn around rather than riding into their setup.

Do not run in a straight line towards the most obvious exit. Change direction sharply and make scouts guess where their group should dismount. If the first pursuer approaches from ahead, reversing towards the route you already cleared is often safer than continuing towards their teammates.

Log out only after breaking contact

Logging out can end a trip after the group has lost you, but it cannot save an active chase. Move away from roads, exits, objectives and the place you were last seen before starting the countdown. Your character remains in the world until it completes, and taking damage or acting cancels the attempt. If pursuers still know the area you are hiding in, keep moving towards a real safe exit instead.

If you are dismounted directly beside a map exit, stall for as long as you safely can before crossing. Going through immediately means your 30-second invulnerability bubble can expire at roughly the same time as your 30-second remount timer, leaving no time to mount and create distance. Waiting before you cross lets the remount timer keep running, so you can mount and move before the bubble expires.

Use the full sequence in a safe zone until the key order is automatic. This reduces the number of decisions you must make under pressure, but it cannot recreate the adrenaline of your first real ganks. Expect panic and some losses while learning. Keep early sets affordable, review one decision after each attempt and do not let a failed escape stop you trying again.

Every gank is different. Record gathering sessions when possible, then review failed escapes for the first warning you missed, your ability order, nearby escape options and whether your route was predictable. You can also submit the recording to the

content: Which resource should I gather first?

children: Every gathering line can be profitable at T8. Start with a resource that is common in the biome connected to your portal city. Hide tends to sell well but requires killing resource mobs, increasing the time spent dismounted. Stone has historically had a weaker early-tier economy but less competition at high tiers. Check

content: Which resources appear in each Albion Online biome?

children: Each open-world biome has a primary, secondary and tertiary resource. Primary resources are the most common, so your portal city and planned route should influence which gathering line you level first.

content: Should I level one gathering line at a time?

children: Yes, if the goal is to reach a specific T8 line quickly. Matching gathering gear adds yield and fame for that resource, so splitting attention before the first line is established slows focused progression. Multiple T8 tools become powerful later because enchanted-node roaming can monetise more of each map.

content: Should I spend Learning Points on gathering?

children: If gathering is a serious progression goal, Learning Points are one of the strongest ways to shorten its slow unlock curve. Reserve them for gathering milestones rather than spending them casually across unrelated trees. Track the plan in

At T6, harvest T4-T6 resources in T6 zones and visit resource hotspots.

Start with an affordable set, decide the carried value that triggers a bank run and judge the method across several trips rather than one death or one exceptional haul. summary: Corrupted Dungeon ratting isn't a new strategy - it's been around since the early days of the mode. I still remember when Black Hands (RIP 24.11.2021), back then part of the dagger weapon tree, were a popular sight in Corrupted Dungeons. What a weapon.

toc.title: Choose Your Corrupted Dungeon Rat Build

children: Corrupted Dungeon ratting isn't a new strategy - it's been around since the early days of the mode. I still remember when Black Hands (RIP 24.11.2021), back then part of the dagger weapon tree, were a popular sight in Corrupted Dungeons. What a weapon.

Builds have changed, but the idea behind ratting remains simple: focus on PvE, open as many chests as efficiently as possible, and escape invasions rather than look for fights. This guide follows that approach, with three builds and a practical four-chest route for farming silver and fame on your way to Slayer.

content: How fast should a Stalker or Slayer run be?

children: Aim for a repeatable 5-6 minute clear. One exceptional speed run is less useful than an average you can sustain across an entire food session. If most clears take much longer, improve the route or build before increasing set cost.

content: How many Corrupted Dungeons should I chain?

children: Aim for five or six dungeons per food. Check the remaining buff timer before chaining because transitions and invasions reduce the number you can finish. Bank earlier when an unusually valuable drop makes the next run a poor risk.

content: How do I progress to Slayer?

children: Practise roughly 5-10 runs in Hunter if needed, then farm Stalker until you reach 100,000 personal Infamy. Slayer also requires 1,100 base IP. Aim for roughly 1,400-1,500 displayed IP before entering and prefer T8.1 Avalonian Beef Stew. Estimate the remaining runs from your measured net Infamy gain, not the boss-progress bar.

content: Which potion should I use for skipping?

children: Use T4 or T6 Poison for clearing, not expensive T8 Poison. For skipping, bring T6/T8 Tornado in a Bottle to knock enemy players away, ideally throwing it into a choke point on the pursuer's route, or T8 Invisibility to break contact. The T8 Poison shown in the build cards is an editor tier limitation, not the recommended farming purchase.

content: When should I kill the second miniboss?

children: Ideally reach 1,600 of 2,000 points in Slayer, or 400 of 500 in Stalker, before killing the second miniboss. These totals include the first miniboss. The second kill adds 400 or 100 respectively, fills the bar and summons the final boss, preventing new invasions. Use this order when it fits the layout without excessive backtracking; it does not remove an active invader.

content: Does boss spawn end an active invasion?

children: No. Boss spawn prevents a new invasion from beginning but does not remove an invader already inside. During an active invasion, destroy three of the five Demonic Shards or take the fight.

content: Is Corrupted Dungeon ratting AFK farming?

children: No. The PvE loop can feel low-interaction once learned, but invasions, traps and lethal deaths require attention while the character is active.
